## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One critical defect needs fixing: `Cache.set` stores keys without lower-casing them, but `get` always looks up the lower-cased key. Any value set under a mixed-case key can never be read back. This review traced the read and write paths in `app/cache.py` against the case-insensitivity contract stated at `app/cache.py:14-15` and read the added tests; it did not run them. `test_entries_expire` is set up correctly: it patches `time.monotonic` on the module that `app/cache.py` resolves at call time, so the expiry branch in `get` is actually exercised.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `Cache.set(key, value)` method that stores a value with an expiry of `time.monotonic() + ttl`. It raises `DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds, updates the matching comment, and adds tests for round trips, the default TTL and expiry.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `c.set("ALPHA", 1)` followed by `c.get("ALPHA")` (or `c.get("alpha")`) returns `None`, because `set` writes `self._store[key]` with the key as given while `get` reads `self._store.get(key.lower())` at `app/cache.py:17`. This breaks the class contract at `app/cache.py:14-15`: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first, or mixed-case callers create duplicate entries that never expire together." `test_set_then_get_round_trip` only sets the already-lowercase `"alpha"`, so it passes despite the defect. — Callers that move from writing `_store` directly to calling `set` lose every mixed-case write without any error. Those entries also never get evicted, because `get` never finds them to run the expiry delete at `app/cache.py:22`, so they stay in memory for the life of the cache. — Fix: Use `self._store[key.lower()] = ...`, and add a test that sets a mixed-case key such as `"Alpha"` and reads it back with a different casing.
